product.amstrad-megapc.summary: A home PC that switched between DOS and Mega Drive cartridges using its front cover.
product.amstrad-megapc.history: Amstrad combined the PC7386SX main unit with a games card under licence from Sega. The Mega PC was aimed at households that wanted a computer for work and a console for games on the same monitor. In January 1993, UK dealer Admincure advertised the complete system for £699 excluding VAT.
product.amstrad-megapc.technical.video: The sliding front cover selected PC or Mega Drive mode. The dual-sync monitor accepted the two modes at 31 and 15 kHz respectively.
product.amstrad-megapc.technical.audio: The manual distinguishes AdLib audio in PC mode from stereo in Mega Drive mode. The games card provided access to Sega cartridges and controllers.
product.amstrad-megapc.warning: Inherited PC profile. Boot and Mega Drive validation pending.
product.amstrad-megapc.technical.firmwar: The preserved PC firmware uses two 64 KiB ROMs, U18 and U19. Interleaving yields 32 KiB of video firmware from offset 0 and 64 KiB of system firmware from offset 0x8000 in each chip.
product.amstrad-megapc.technical.verifie: Static analysis confirmed the checksums and the AMSTRAD PC7386SX string in the system block. The BluMach code includes the PC profile with WD76C10 and WD90C11 graphics.
product.amstrad-megapc.technical.limitat: PC boot and peripherals remain to be validated. The current profile covers the PC side. The Mega Drive card and video and audio switching require dedicated work.
